summary: MaterialDNA schema-v2 numeric-bound gap: maintenance.repairCount is validated only as a finite non-negative integer, with no upper bound, while the production contract states numeric plausibility ranges are finite and bounded. This leaves one canonical recipe integer outside the otherwise bounded domain. A narrow source-only closure should cap repairCount at a deterministic 31-bit non-negative maximum and add an oversized-count regression without changing MaterialId, recipeVersion, schemaVersion, state, or fixture identity semantics.
evidence: src/shared/Materials/MaterialDNA.luau: validateMaintenance calls validateNonNegativeInteger for maintenance.repairCount; validateNonNegativeInteger has no maximum parameter/check.
src/shared/Materials/MaterialDNA.luau: other canonical numeric plausibility fields use explicit finite ranges/maxima, and recipeVersion is capped at 2147483647.
Docs/MATERIAL_DNA_CONTRACT.md: validation contract says numeric plausibility ranges are finite and bounded.
tests/materialdna_contract.luau: recipeVersion has an oversized-value regression, but maintenance.repairCount has no equivalent bound regression.
